name: Intercontinental Exchange
description: ICE runs exchanges and clearing houses (energy futures, the New York Stock Exchange and other U.S. equity and options venues), sells market data and fixed-income pricing and analytics, and sells software to mortgage lenders and servicers. Net revenue of $9.9 billion in 2025 was 54 percent exchanges, 24 percent fixed income and data, 21 percent mortgage technology. Exchanges earn per-contract and per-share fees that rise with volume; data and mortgage software are largely recurring subscriptions. Exchanges alone produced 81 percent of segment operating income.

employees.note: 12,844 total: 7,551 in the U.S., 5,293 international (3,512 in India) (10-K).

businessLines.name: Exchanges
businessLines.how: Per-contract and per-share trading and clearing fees on futures (energy 2,182 gross, agricultural and metals 233, financial 608), cash equities and equity options (3,176), plus data, connectivity and listing fees (1,031 and 495); volumes and volatility drive it.

revenue.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), revenues less transaction-based expenses

businessLines.name: Fixed Income and Data Services
businessLines.how: Subscriptions to fixed-income pricing, reference data, indices and analytics (1,234), plus CDS clearing fees (338) and fixed-income execution (125), and a global network and desktop data (722 computed remainder).

businessLines.name: Mortgage Technology
businessLines.how: Software subscriptions and per-loan fees charged to lenders and servicers for origination technology (738), servicing software (871), closing solutions (223) and data and analytics (269); volumes follow mortgage activity. Near-zero operating margin reflects heavy amortisation and integration costs.
